queue.title: When Two Reps Define 'Proposal Sent' Differently, Who's Right?
queue.brief: Explores how inconsistent stage definitions between reps corrupt pipeline data in monday.com, and how a CRM audit exposes the problem before it distorts your forecast.
queue.description: H2 sections: Why stage names mean nothing without exit criteria; The two reps, two definitions problem in monday.com; What the audit reveals (stage distribution skew, field completeness gaps by rep, stale deals piling in one stage); How to write a one-line exit criterion for each stage; Making the fix stick without a team training day. Target keyword: monday.com pipeline stage consistency. Concrete example: two reps both use 'Proposal Sent' — one moves a deal there the moment a deck is shared, the other waits for a formal quote with a signed NDA; the CRM Audit flags a lopsided stage distribution and near-zero field completeness in that stage, revealing the discrepancy.
